text.p: Australia's Rodney Eyles, beaten in the last two finals of the Qatar International by world champion Jansher Khan, qualified for the second round of this year's tournament by winning a bad-tempered match against Egypt's Ahmed Faizy on Sunday.
Eyles, the world number two, defeated the Egyptian world junior champion 15-9 15-14 15-13 in 49 minutes.
The match was marred in the early stages by a succession of complaints from both players, while Faizy was warned for wasting time.
At one stage, Eyles complained to referee Bernhard Sartor that he was in danger of being hit in the face by Faizy's racket.
"It's just my swing," retorted the Egyptian.
The mood of the match improved later when Eyles jokingly lifted his lightweight opponent and carried him across the court.
After the match, Eyles played down the unsavoury aspects of the game.

"There is no malice between us out there. In different situations, we have different ways of playing," said Eyles, who caused a major surprise in August when he defeated Jansher in the final of the Hong Kong Open.
Australia's world number three Brett Martin claimed his place in the next round without lifting a racket when Simon Frenz of Germany was forced to withdraw because of an ankle injury.
England's Chris Walker struggled through against Egyptian school student Amr Shabana 15-11 13-15 15-9 15-13.

Crowds for the tournament have been disappointingly low even though it features the world's top players. Only 25 people watched the last match of the day between England pair Jason Nicolle and Tim Garner. The stadium has a capacity of 1,000.
